facts: Challenge in this appeal is to the judgment of a Division Bench of the Andhra Pradesh High Court allowing the appeal filed by the State so far as present appellant is concerned while upholding the acquittal of other accused persons.

The earned IV Additional Sessions Judge, Guntur had directed acquittal of all the five accused persons who faced trial for commission of offence punishable u/s. 302 and S. 302 read with S. 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (in short the 'IPC').
The State filed an appeal in terms of S. 378(1) and (3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (in short the 'Code').
issues: Whether the High Court has applied its mind to the various aspects and the position in law as highlighted above relating to the scope for interference in appeal against an order of acquittal.
petitioner_arguments: The High Court has not discussed the evidence of the witnesses and has come to abrupt conclusions about the acceptability of the evidence.
There is no embargo on the appellate Court reviewing the evidence upon which an order of acquittal is based.
respondent_arguments: Though the High Court has not analysed the evidence in detail, its conclusions are not erroneous.
court_reasoning: The golden thread which runs through the web of administration of justice in criminal cases is that if two views are possible on the evidence adduced in the case, one pointing to the guilt of the accused and the other to his innocence, the view which is favourable to the accused should be adopted.
A miscarriage of justice which may arise from acquittal of the guilty is no less than from the conviction of an innocent.
holding: The appeal filed by the State is allowed as far as A 1 is concerned. A 1 is convicted and sentenced to suffer imprisonment for life and he is directed to surrender forthwith.
The appeal filed by the State against A 2 to A 5 stands dismissed.
